Fit the short-term trend of every draw of a csfmt_ensemble_v4

Source: R/v4_trend.R
short_term_trend_v4.Rd

Fits a rolling quasi-Poisson regression of measure on the week index in every draw. With denominator, the fit is the rate model measure ~ t + offset(log(denominator)).

Usage

short_term_trend_v4(
  x,
  measure,
  width = 3,
  denominator = NULL,
  name = measure,
  seed
)

Arguments

x

The csfmt_ensemble_v4, full or compressed.

measure

The name of the draw matrix of counts in $draws.

width

The number of weeks in a window, one whole number of at least 2.

denominator

NULL for a count, or the name of the draw matrix of the denominator for a rate.

name

The start of the new names. It MUST NOT end in a reserved suffix, and each new name MUST be at most 63 bytes.

seed

The seed of the t draws, one whole number.

Value

x with the new draw matrices <name>_trend_beta1 and <name>_trend_se, and these new columns in $data:

  • <name>_trend_pinc: P(increasing).

  • <name>_trend_gr: the median growth rate.

  • <name>_trend_gr_q02x5 to <name>_trend_gr_q97x5: the growth rate at the 9 percentiles 2.5, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95 and 97.5.

A rerun with the same name replaces these draw matrices and columns.

Details

The window of a week holds that week and the width - 1 weeks before it. The time t is the week index, so the slope is a change of the log mean per week. The fit is that of stats::glm() with the quasi-Poisson family, and the dispersion has no floor.

Each series MUST have one row per ISO week, from its first week to its last, as the output of nowcast_passthrough_v4() has. The function reads the weeks from x$time_col. It stops with an error that names the series and the two weeks around the gap when a week is missing or repeated. It also stops when x$time_col holds a value that is not an ISO week. A week with no count MUST be a row with NA.

A row with an NA count or denominator leaves the window. A zero denominator becomes 1 before the log, as in the v1 method. The first of these rules that holds for a window, in one draw, decides its values:

  • Rule 3. A window with NA rows and fewer than 3 rows left gets NA.

  • Rule 2. A window where every count left is 0 gets P(increasing) 0, and NA slope, standard error and growth rate.

  • Rule 4. A window gets NA when its fit does not converge, has a non-finite value, or has separated counts. The fit needs 3 rows, so a window of width 2 with a count above 0 also gets NA.

  • Every other window gets the slope and standard error of its fit.

The first width - 1 weeks of each series have no window and get NA.

P(increasing) is the mean over draws j of pt(beta1_j / se_j, df_j). Here df_j is the number of rows left in the window minus 2. A draw with NA leaves the mean, and the mean of no draws is NA.

The growth rate is 100 * (exp(b_j) - 1) percent per week, with b_j = beta1_j + se_j * t_j. Each draw gets one t_j from the t distribution with df_j degrees of freedom. The percentiles are over the draws. With one draw, the function draws no random number: the percentile p is then 100 * (exp(beta1 + se * qt(p, df)) - 1).

The function sets seed itself, and then puts back the random-number state of the caller.

See also

Other v4 functions: as_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_ensemble_v4(), csfmt_reporting_triangle_v4(), ens_add_rate_v4(), ens_compress_v4(), mem_thresholds_v4(), nowcast_ecdf_v4(), nowcast_passthrough_v4(), print.csfmt_ensemble_v4(), signal_detection_hlm_v4()

Examples

d <- data.table::data.table(
  location_code = "nation",
  isoyearweek = sprintf("2023-%02d", 1:10)
)
set.seed(1)
ens <- csfmt_ensemble_v4(
  d,
  id_cols = "location_code",
  draws = list(cases = matrix(rpois(10 * 200, 20 * exp(0.1 * 1:10)), 10))
)
ens <- short_term_trend_v4(ens, measure = "cases", width = 5, seed = 4)
ens$data[, .(isoyearweek, cases_trend_pinc, cases_trend_gr)]
#>     isoyearweek cases_trend_pinc cases_trend_gr
#>          <char>            <num>          <num>
#>  1:     2023-01               NA             NA
#>  2:     2023-02               NA             NA
#>  3:     2023-03               NA             NA
#>  4:     2023-04               NA             NA
#>  5:     2023-05        0.8524386      10.695048
#>  6:     2023-06        0.8526068       8.954959
#>  7:     2023-07        0.8814534      10.461606
#>  8:     2023-08        0.8729255       9.832097
#>  9:     2023-09        0.9110734      11.319846
